title: A Fragile New Start After Ruin
overview: After Jerusalem falls, Jeremiah is freed and joins Gedaliah, the new local governor, whose hopeful fresh start is threatened by a murder plot he refuses to believe.

parts.label: Freed by the enemy (vv. 1-4)
parts.note: Jeremiah had been swept up in chains with the captives, and the Babylonian commander released him at Ramah, a town north of Jerusalem. Strikingly, this foreign officer repeats Jeremiah's own message back to him: the city fell because its people ignored God's warnings.

parts.label: Jeremiah chooses to stay (vv. 5-6)
parts.note: Offered comfort in Babylon, Jeremiah instead went to Gedaliah at Mizpah, a town just north of Jerusalem, to live among the poor left behind. Gedaliah came from a family that had protected Jeremiah before, and the commander sent him off with food and a gift.

parts.label: Gedaliah's promise (vv. 7-10)
parts.note: Judah's army officers had been hiding in the countryside, likely afraid Babylon would punish them. Gedaliah swore that if they accepted Babylonian rule and worked the land, they would be safe, and he would deal with the Babylonians himself.

parts.label: The scattered come home (vv. 11-12)
parts.note: Jews who had fled to neighboring nations like Moab, Ammon and Edom heard there was order again and returned. That year they gathered a large harvest, a small sign of life returning to a ruined land.

parts.label: A warning ignored (vv. 13-16)
parts.note: Johanan warned that Ishmael, a man of royal descent, had been sent by the king of Ammon to kill Gedaliah, and offered to kill Ishmael first in secret. Gedaliah refused to believe it, and the next chapter shows the warning was true.

think: When someone warns you about a person you trust, how do you decide whether to believe them?
